subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Your Rajni bua was fifteen once, you know. There was a boy in my tuition, Vishal. For three months he was my whole world. Then, slowly, I got bored. Not of him exactly, but of the same phone calls every night, the same "what are you doing now?"
But I didn't say that. I hinted. I said I had exams. I said Ma was strict about the phone. I took longer and longer to reply, hoping he'd understand.
He didn't understand. He felt me slipping, so he called more. He waited outside tuition every day, even when I'd said I had to rush home. He sent me songs with sad lyrics. And every time he needed me more, I felt more trapped and pulled further away.
It was like a knot that tightens when you pull. I should have told him honestly what I felt. Instead we both spent a month going round and round.

qa.q: Where did Vishal wait every day?
qa.a: Vishal waited outside tuition every day.

qa.q: Why did Rajni take longer to reply instead of speaking up?
qa.a: Rajni felt bored and trapped but didn't want to hurt Vishal, so she hinted, hoping he would understand.

qa.q: What could Rajni have done to loosen the knot?
qa.a: Rajni could have told Vishal honestly that she needed space or felt differently, instead of hints that left him confused and more anxious.

qa.q: What was Vishal experiencing as Rajni slipped away?
qa.a: Vishal sensed the change without being told why, so he felt anxious and clung harder, calling more and waiting outside tuition.

grounding: Shows a teen who feels bored and trapped hinting instead of speaking, while her boyfriend clings harder and pushes her further away.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
The school bus to Mahabaleshwar lost network every few kilometres, and Payal was secretly glad. Aman had called four times since breakfast.
"Network's bad," she texted when a bar came back. It was true, but not the whole truth.
Vandana, squashed beside her, watched Payal's phone light up again. "u ok? why so quiet? did I do something?" Then: "call me when u reach. pls. pls."
Payal turned the phone face down. She wasn't angry at him. She just felt something pressing on her chest whenever his name appeared. She didn't know how to say "I think I'm bored" without it sounding cruel.
"You're not replying?" Vandana asked.
"Later," Payal said, and looked out at the hills. Behind her silence, she knew, Aman was getting more worried, and more worry meant more messages, and more messages made her want to disappear.

qa.q: How many times had Aman called since breakfast?
qa.a: Aman had called four times since breakfast.

qa.q: What is Payal feeling when Aman's name appears?
qa.a: Payal feels a pressure on her chest, bored and trapped, and doesn't know how to say it without sounding cruel.

qa.q: What could Payal do to stop the cycle of hints and worried messages?
qa.a: When she's back, Payal could tell Aman honestly and gently that her feelings have changed or that she needs space, instead of using the bad network as cover.

qa.q: How is Aman experiencing Payal's silence?
qa.a: Aman senses a change, worries he did something wrong and sends more messages, which only pushes Payal further away.

grounding: Illustrates a teen feeling bored and trapped who hints rather than speaks, while the other's growing need pushes her further away.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Monday. Chinmay told his friend Madhav that he was "just tired of things" with Ritika. He didn't say he was bored. When Ritika messaged "movie on Saturday?", he replied, "Maybe, lots of homework."

Wednesday, two days later. Ritika sensed something. She messaged more, sent him songs, asked three times if he was okay. Chinmay felt the phone buzz in his pocket during maths and didn't take it out. Each buzz made him feel more trapped.

Saturday, that weekend. He skipped the movie, saying his cousin was visiting. Ritika sent: "Did I do something wrong? Please tell me." He stared at it for ten minutes and wrote, "No, all good 🙂". He knew it wasn't.

Madhav, who was with him, said, "You're not being fair to her."

Chinmay pushed the phone away. "I know. I just don't know how to say it."

qa.q: What excuse did Chinmay give for skipping the movie?
qa.a: That his cousin was visiting.

qa.q: How does Chinmay feel each time his phone buzzes in maths?
qa.a: He feels more trapped and uncomfortable, bored with the relationship but not saying so.

qa.q: What could Chinmay do instead of hinting?
qa.a: He could tell Ritika honestly and kindly how he feels, so she isn't left guessing and messaging more.

qa.q: What is it like for Ritika to get "No, all good" after asking if she did something wrong?
qa.a: She probably feels confused and anxious, sensing a change but getting mixed signals, which makes her cling harder.

grounding: Over a week Chinmay feels bored and trapped and hints instead of speaking, while Ritika senses the change and clings harder, pushing him further away.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Sumit, you asked me why you should just tell that girl how you feel. Let me tell you about me and Rosa, when I was sixteen in Kochi. Your Joseph uncle wasn't always so wise.

We'd been together six months. Then I started feeling bored. Nothing was wrong. I just didn't want to see her every day. But I didn't say that. I said, "I'm busy." I stopped calling first. I went to the beach with the boys and didn't tell her.

Rosa noticed. She started waiting outside my tuition. She wrote me notes. She asked my sister what was wrong. And every time she did, I felt more trapped and pulled further away.

The turning point came when she cried in front of the church after Sunday mass and asked, "Just tell me." I finally did. It hurt her. But it hurt less than the three months of hints before it.

qa.q: Where did Rosa start waiting for Joseph?
qa.a: Outside his tuition.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel each time Rosa wrote him notes or waited for him?
qa.a: He felt more trapped and pulled further away, bored but unable to say it.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: When Rosa cried after Sunday mass and asked him to just tell her, and he finally told the truth.

qa.q: How might Rosa have felt during those three months of hints?
qa.a: She probably felt anxious and confused, sensing a change and clinging harder because no one told her what was wrong.

grounding: Joseph uncle recalls feeling bored and hinting instead of speaking, while his girlfriend sensed the change and clung harder, pushing him further away.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
It was the week of the school annual day, and Aparna had rehearsals every evening and a stack of costumes to finish. She didn't have time for anything, which was almost a relief, because it gave her an excuse.

Nikhil had started to feel like a weight. She didn't know why. He hadn't done anything wrong. She just felt restless when he held her hand in the corridor.

So she hinted. "I'm so busy." "Let's talk after annual day." "I need some me-time."

Nikhil noticed. He started turning up at rehearsals with snacks. He messaged every hour: "You okay?" "Miss you." "Did I annoy you?" Each message made Aparna's chest tighter.

Her friend Tanuja watched it all from the costume table. "You're sending mixed signals," she said.

"I know," Aparna said. "But if I tell him, it's over."

qa.q: What was Aparna busy with that week?
qa.a: Rehearsals every evening and a stack of costumes to finish for the annual day.

qa.q: What does Aparna's tightening chest suggest about how she feels?
qa.a: It suggests she feels trapped and guilty, restless in the relationship but afraid to say so.

qa.q: What would you advise Aparna?
qa.a: To speak honestly and kindly to Nikhil soon, rather than hinting, because the mixed signals are making him cling harder.

qa.q: How does Nikhil see Aparna's busyness?
qa.a: He senses something has changed and worries he annoyed her, so he tries harder with snacks and messages.

grounding: During a busy school week Aparna feels trapped and hints rather than speaking, while Nikhil senses a change and clings harder.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
After tuition, Jagdish walked slower than usual so that Sonal would reach the bus stop first. She didn't; she waited for him under the neem tree.
"You didn't call last night," she said.
"Tired," he said, which was partly true. What he couldn't say was that their nightly calls had started to feel like homework he had never chosen. On Saturday he had hinted, "Maybe we both need more time with friends?" and she had laughed and texted him twice as often.
Now she held out a keychain she had made with his initials. "For your bag."
He took it, said "Nice," and felt worse.
His friend Omkar, who had watched from the tea stall, asked later, "Are you two okay?"
Jagdish shrugged. "She's too much these days."
Omkar looked at him for a moment. "Or are you just not saying something?"

qa.q: What did Sonal give Jagdish at the bus stop?
qa.a: She gave him a keychain she had made with his initials, for his bag.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling when he took the keychain and said 'Nice'?
qa.a: He felt guilty and trapped, because the calls had come to feel like unchosen homework, yet he could not bring himself to say so.

qa.q: What could help break this cycle of hints and clinging?
qa.a: Jagdish could say plainly and kindly what he feels instead of hinting about more time with friends, so Sonal is not left guessing and holding on harder.

qa.q: What is it like for Sonal when Jagdish goes quiet and slow?
qa.a: Sonal senses a change without knowing what it is, so she waits, asks about the missed call and makes him a gift, trying to hold on.

grounding: Shows a teen who feels bored and trapped hinting instead of speaking, while the partner senses a change and becomes clingier.
